clue.text: Seven stars, and one who eats a lot of chips?

definitions.text: one who eats a lot of chips?

blocks.note: first meaning: the bright seven-star pattern in Ursa Major

blocks.clueFragment: one who eats a lot of chips?
blocks.note: second meaning, playful: someone who dunks many chips in salsa or dip

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey literal reading: a heavy snacker at the dip bowl is a 'big dipper'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Dipper is the American name for the seven-star asterism also called the Plough.

clue.text: Bring up bookcase's top joint

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so only the initial is used

blocks.note: first letter of bookcase
a roach is the butt of a cannabis joint

explanation.surface: Pull up the top of the bookshelf joint, as in carpentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests woodwork beside 'bookcase', but it is the drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for discussion.

clue.text: Gee — lacking capital, port city north of Maine takes a step to produce opera

indicators.note: capital here is the head letter, which is dropped
in a down answer, north means placed above, so earlier

blocks.note: Gee is the spelled-out name of the letter
the great Dutch port
the US postal abbreviation for Maine
a rung is a step on a ladder

explanation.surface: An exclamation, a broke Dutch port and a step up from Maine combine into a stage work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gee' looks like an exclamation but is the letter G; 'capital' is the first letter, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Götterdämmerung is the final opera of Wagner's Ring cycle, its umlauts dropped in the grid.

clue.text: Versatile Roman in triathlon

indicators.note: versatile means able to take many forms, so the letters adopt a new form

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An all-round Roman athlete competes in a three-part race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the Roman in the race, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironman is a long-distance triathlon of swimming, cycling and running, and the brand name of the event.

clue.text: Harshly criticize folds in certain body parts

blocks.note: a critic who pans a show savages it
creases are folds

explanation.surface: Slamming the wrinkles in parts of the body, as in a harsh cosmetic review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it places folds inside body parts; here it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is an abdominal gland; certain body parts in the plural are pancreases.

clue.text: Wander around with Bush's brain

blocks.note: first meaning: to roam
second meaning: Karl ..., the strategist nicknamed Bush's Brain

explanation.walkthrough: Karl Rove was George W. Bush's chief political adviser, so widely credited with Bush's strategy that a book called him 'Bush's Brain'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to wander without fixed course, and Rove is the adviser's surname.

clue.text: Following a revolution, Chinese factory contains places to get a drink

indicators.note: the phrase that follows holds the letters within it, running across the word break
a revolution turns something round, so the concealed letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second, read in order

explanation.surface: A Chinese factory, after some political upheaval, now houses bars.
explanation.walkthrough: chineSE FACtory holds SEFAC, which turned round gives CAFES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafés are establishments serving coffee and other beverages, so they are spots for a drink.

clue.text: Conversation on French water for mansion

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above the next piece

blocks.note: a chat is an informal conversation
eau is the French word for water

explanation.surface: Talking over a glass of French water at a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a large French country house or castle, hence a mansion.

clue.text: Henry, a reference will briefly be heard as pertaining to space-time

indicators.note: be heard means the words are judged by how they come out of the mouth, not their spelling

blocks.note: Henry Ford, a mention, and will shortened to the contraction 'll, run together

explanation.surface: A hint that a reference from Henry will be cited about Einstein's physics.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is Henry Ford, the carmaker; 'briefly' trims will to the contraction 'll. Said quickly, Ford-a-mention'll approximates four-dimensional.
explanation.definitionFit: Space-time combines three spatial dimensions with time, making a four-dimensional continuum.

clue.text: Stitching up rising American computer scientist

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: US is short for American
Alan Turing, the pioneer of computer science

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming American computer scientist is sewing something together.
explanation.definitionFit: Suturing is the surgical act of closing a wound with stitches.

clue.text: Exhausted couple enters our cabin at the rear

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the next, as a person entering a room ends up within it
only the hindmost letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: a couple is a pair
taken as written
the final letter of cabin

explanation.surface: A tired pair crawls into the back of our cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' looks like it describes the couple, but it is the definition; the couple is simply the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Outworn means used up or worn out, a close synonym of exhausted.

clue.text: Elevated roadway cut catastrophically after 6 CE

indicators.note: something wrecked catastrophically is thrown into disorder, so the word before it is jumbled
tells us the jumbled piece is placed behind the other parts

blocks.note: six in Roman numerals
CE (Common Era) is the same dating span as AD
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A raised road was destroyed in a disaster shortly after the year 6 CE.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6' is not a cross-reference to 6 Across; read it as a Roman numeral. CE and AD label the same years.
explanation.definitionFit: A viaduct is a long bridge carrying a road or railway high over a valley.

clue.text: Weep about stack of paper at the back of the dairy

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps the material that follows
only the last letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: to weep is to cry
a ream is a 500-sheet bundle of paper
final letter of the

explanation.surface: Someone sobs over a pile of paperwork behind the milk shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the dairy' looks like one phrase, but 'the' supplies a letter and 'dairy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamery is an establishment where milk, butter and cheese are produced or sold.

clue.text: Mailer's Terminator

blocks.note: the possessive ending supplies its letter
a terminator is something that ends things

explanation.surface: It reads like a reference to novelist Norman Mailer's killing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mailer' looks like the writer Norman Mailer, but it simply means one who mails; the apostrophe-s is a letter of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever posts a letter or parcel is its sender.

clue.text: Armies beginning to tangle in blood-spattered, terrifying tale

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word means only its opening letter
in places the preceding pieces inside the word that follows

blocks.note: gory means covered in blood
hosts is an old word for armies
first letter of tangle

explanation.surface: Troops start to fight in a bloody, frightening story.
explanation.walkthrough: Hosts is an archaic or biblical word for armies, as in 'Lord of hosts'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost story is a spooky narrative of hauntings meant to frighten.

clue.text: Paradise is an Internet lair?

blocks.note: E as in e-mail, e-commerce: the prefix for electronic or Internet
an animal's lair is its den

explanation.surface: A wry claim that heaven is just an online hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits E for Internet is a stretch: it is the prefix in e-mail and e-business.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the garden of Genesis, used generally for any place of perfect bliss.

clue.text: British poet rebuilt home sauna

indicators.note: something rebuilt has had its parts put together in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A British poet has renovated the steam room at his house.
explanation.walkthrough: A. E. Housman wrote A Shropshire Lad; his initials are part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Edward Housman was an English classical scholar and lyric poet.

clue.text: Saint overrides call to hang

indicators.note: over means placed above in a down answer, so the first piece rides on top

blocks.note: St. is the standard abbreviation for Saint
to ring up is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A saint overrules the order to execute someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overrides' reads as overruling, but split it: the saint rides over the call.
explanation.definitionFit: To string someone up is to hang them, especially by a lynch mob.

clue.text: Femme fatale's wig?

blocks.note: first meaning: a seductive, dangerous woman
second meaning, punning: split as ..., a temporary lock of hair

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the joke: a wig is hair you wear for a while, a 'temp tress'.
explanation.definitionFit: A temptress is a woman who seduces or lures, the classic femme fatale.

clue.text: Device that provides heat to a flower

blocks.note: taken as written
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A gadget that keeps a bloom warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is a kitchen appliance that browns bread with heated elements.

clue.text: NRA obsession is comfortable, if you think backwards

indicators.note: thinking backwards means reading the word from its end to its start

blocks.note: snug means cosy and comfortable

explanation.surface: A jibe that the gun lobby's fixation only seems cosy if you think in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comfortable' wants to be the definition; it is the wordplay, and the gun lobby is the definition. The NRA is the US National Rifle Association.
explanation.definitionFit: The National Rifle Association campaigns above all for firearms, so weapons are its fixation.

clue.text: Terrible danger looms over Eastern potentate

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the word after it is scrambled
in a down answer, looming over means sitting above the next piece

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A dreadful threat hangs over an oriental ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern potentate' wants to be read together as the definition; Eastern only supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a nobleman of the highest rank or any person of great power.

clue.text: Man took a spill… ouch!

blocks.note: to take a spill is to fall over
an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A guy tumbles over and cries out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as the subject who fell, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow is an informal word for a man or chap.

clue.text: Melting ice cap? It makes you want to throw up

definitions.text: It makes you want to throw up

indicators.note: melting things lose their shape, so these letters reform in a new order

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Climate anxiety: the shrinking polar ice is enough to make you sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac syrup is a plant-derived emetic once given to induce vomiting after poisoning.

clue.text: Element of Asian Tet offensive

indicators.note: an offensive is an assault, and these words are attacked and broken up

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A part of the 1968 Tet Offensive in the Vietnam War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tet Offensive' reads as one historical name, but 'offensive' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare radioactive halogen, chemical element number 85.

clue.text: Elitist bastard grabs the last piece of bacon

indicators.note: grabbing takes something into one's hold, so one piece goes inside
only the final letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: SOB is short for son of a bitch
final letter of bacon

explanation.surface: A stuck-up jerk snatches the final rasher.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on people thought socially inferior, an elitist attitude.

clue.text: Pig's belly holding second serving of slop (a large amount)

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside, so one piece goes within another
the second helping means the letter in second position of the next word

blocks.note: the belly is the gut
second letter of slop
a ton of something is a great deal

explanation.surface: A hog's stomach swells with another ladle of swill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig's belly' looks like one phrase, but 'Pig' alone is the definition: G(L)UT then TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a pig means they overeat, which is exactly what a glutton does.

clue.text: Arnold going nuts around the first, second, or third

indicators.note: someone going nuts loses their composure, so the name is scrambled
the scrambled name wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange
first is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Arnold loses it over who came first, second or third.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'first' does double duty: it is part of the definition and also supplies the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are ordinal numbers, giving position in a sequence rather than quantity.

clue.text: Mature during promotion for radio receiver

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to mature is to age
PR is public relations, promotional work

explanation.surface: Growing up in the middle of an ad campaign for a radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager, or beeper, is a small device that receives short radio messages.

clue.text: Lad gets side dish after company leaves — that describes one of nature's inverse relationships

indicators.note: places the second piece behind the first
leaves means departs, so those letters are taken out of the dish

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
a cabbage salad served on the side
Co. is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A boy receives salad once the guests depart, which somehow illustrates a law of physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyle's law states that a gas's pressure varies inversely with its volume at constant temperature.
